requirement.title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement.text:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story: Adds a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute. The generator then writes a formatter, either contractless or driven by a surrogate, into a user-declared partial class for a type from another assembly, and registers it in GeneratedMessagePackResolver.

decisions.title: Dependency change in Directory.Packages.props
decisions.oneliner: Dependency and toolchain versions decide which users can build and run the package.
decisions.question: Accept this dependency or toolchain change?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'dependency': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: Public API change in Attributes.cs
decisions.oneliner: New public types become a promise to every user of the package and cannot be removed without a breaking release.
decisions.question: Add GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute to the public API?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'public-api': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: Immutable types silently serialize nothing
decisions.oneliner: Get-only and constructor-only members are dropped with no diagnostic. A record-like type compiles fine and round-trips to empty objects.
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: Some other diagnostic already fires when a generated formatter ends up with zero members or skips public members.
decisions.question: Should the generator warn when it skips public get-only members, or when it finds no serializable members?

handled.title: Surrogate design differs from requested options
handled.oneliner: The issue offered three options: DataMember, user-copied attribute definitions, or generated attributes. The agent built a fourth: a surrogate type in Project B.
quote: To control keys and membership without touching the type, name a *surrogate* type in the attribute.
handled.requirement_part: As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives
handled.would_be_wrong_if: Maintainers already agreed on the surrogate approach in the issue thread.
handled.question: Is a surrogate type an acceptable replacement for the three options the requester listed, given it doesn't support Union?
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: No duplicate check for the same data type
handled.oneliner: Nothing stops a second formatter or a [MessagePackObject] model for the same T. Both get added to the resolver, which can give conflicting or broken output.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The model merge or the resolver template already deduplicates ObjectInfos by DataType.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Wrong args passed to existing diagnostics
handled.oneliner: NoDeserializingConstructor and MemberNeedsKey are reused with different arguments than their message formats may expect. Mismatched placeholders could throw or print garbled text.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: NoDeserializingConstructor's messageFormat has no {n} placeholders (the descriptor is not in the diff).
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Symbols cached in incremental pipeline, collected twice
handled.oneliner: GeneratedFormatterRequest holds INamedTypeSymbols, which breaks incremental caching. Collect also runs twice per formatter, which slows the IDE.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The existing pipeline already passes symbols the same way and maintainers accept the cost.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Untested rejection paths
handled.oneliner: No tests cover generic or inaccessible data types (MsgPack021), the missing-ctor error, or the init-only and required member paths.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

not_checked: The test suite was not run (no .NET SDK on the review host).
Whether EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces emits the right modifiers when the user's formatter is nested in another type or namespace
Whether the separate MessagePackAnalyzer package (not the generator) is expected to report MsgPack019–022, since Initialize is unchanged
Whether the init-only and required members selected here deserialize correctly through the existing template without constructor parameters
